subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should direct first installs from arbitrary sources require this explicit acknowledgement while ClawHub, bundled, official-catalog, update, repair, setup, and onboarding flows remain warning-free?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes executable-code trust policy and breaks previously valid unattended commands, so repository owners must approve both the trusted-source definition and exempt workflow set.

options.title: Approve after proposal fix
options.body: Keep the proposed trust boundary and acknowledgement flag, repair proposal-only host rendering, and require focused fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to warning-only
options.body: Show provenance warnings but preserve existing noninteractive behavior until a separately approved breaking-policy transition is designed.

options.title: Pause the policy change
options.body: Leave current install behavior unchanged while maintainers define a smaller trust and migration contract.

recommendation.title: Approve after proposal fix
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed trust boundary and acknowledgement flag, repair proposal-only host rendering, and require focused fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history connects this person to both the plugin-install command boundary and the affected Crestodian paths.
